content: 1. It is highly recommended to always fill in the Edit Summary field when making changes to a page. This practice helps both you and other contributors understand the nature of the changes, especially when reviewing the page's history. 2. You can configure your user preferences to prompt you to enter an edit summary if you leave it blank. 3. Always provide an edit summary, even if it is brief. A short summary is better than none at all. This is particularly important when deleting text, as failing to explain the deletion may lead others to assume you are acting in bad faith. 4. If you make multiple changes, mention all significant ones in the summary. If you cannot list them all, you can add and misc. to indicate there are additional changes. 5. Accurate edit summaries help others decide whether they need to review the changes. They can also attract the attention of contributors with expertise in the subject matter. 6. For minor changes, such as fixing spelling errors, a simple note like fixed spelling is sufficient. Even for small edits, providing a summary is courteous and helpful. 7. The edit summary box has a character limit of 200. If you attempt to paste or type more than 200 characters, only the first 200 will be saved, and the rest will be truncated. 8. If you are adding a small amount of text to an article, it is recommended to copy the full text of the addition into the edit summary. This provides maximum information with minimal effort and reduces the need for others to check the page itself. 9. For additions longer than 200 characters, you should write a concise summary of the changes. Alternatively, you can paste the full addition into the summary box, knowing that only the first 200 characters will be saved. 10. The edit summary box only supports one line of text. If you need to include multiple lines, you can manually combine them into a single line before pasting them into the summary box. 11. If the reason for your edit is not clear, it is more likely to be reverted, especially if text has been deleted. In such cases, you can provide a more detailed explanation on the Talk page and reference it in the edit summary with see Talk. 12. Once an edit is saved, the edit summary cannot be changed. To correct errors or omissions in the summary, you can make a dummy edit and include the corrected summary. 13. Edit summaries appear in several places, including the page history, user contributions, watchlists, diff pages, recent changes, and Wikipedia IRC channels. They are also visible in the list of new pages and related changes. 14. Experienced users often use abbreviations in edit summaries to save time, such as rv for revert. While these are generally acceptable for minor edits, they should be used cautiously to avoid confusing new users. 15. The Wikimedia search function does not index edit summaries, and they are not searchable via external search engines. 16. When uploading an image, you can provide an upload summary. This serves as part of the edit summary in the upload log and as text in the image history. It can also describe the image, include links, call templates, or specify categories. 17. The upload summary box has a character limit of 250. However, in the upload log, the last part of the summary may be truncated if it exceeds 255 characters, including the automatically generated uploaded 'filename' text. 18. When adding a new section to a discussion page using the + button, the section title becomes the edit summary. If editing an existing section, the section title is automatically included at the beginning of the summary, enclosed in /and / marks. 19. If you provide a long edit summary, you can delete the automatically included section title to stay within the 200-character limit. Links to sections in edit summaries appear in grey and can be clicked to navigate directly to the section. 20. The Post a comment feature on Talk pages allows you to create a new thread. The text entered in the Subject/headline field becomes both the edit summary and the heading for the new section. 21. In some cases, an automatic edit summary is generated when no summary is provided. While these summaries can provide context, they are not a substitute for a meaningful, user-written summary. 22. Internal links, including piped and interwiki links, are rendered in edit summaries. This makes it preferable to copy wikitext into the summary box rather than plain text from the preview, as it preserves the link formatting. 23. Other wikitext, such as templates or formatting codes, is not interpreted in edit summaries. When copying external links into the summary box, the rendered link and its URL are included, along with a sequential number if applicable.
